items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: we had Booker Pittman... when Booker Pittman came from South America later we recorded that for Columbia

ctx.x: Claude-- what was Claude's last name? Claude Smith? Claude-- oh, could this guy play the violin! And we featured the violin back in those days, also, and we had Booker Pittman. We had John R. Davis, the drummer. Most of these guys were the original guys from when I went to school with, because they were all proficient by this time. And --
So now you're up there at Saint Joseph, Missouri. When did you get into Kansas City?

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: she was our music instructor at high school

ctx.x: And when he would get to the house he would start humming bricks through the window, breaking panes, whizroom, blay-lay-lay-lay whrrrr, bam, bam, bam. Then they'd -- cause he was going to fight his old man. His old man used to fight him, like he was fighting a stranger. He'd fight him -- he whupped the kids with his fists. He never used a strap. He used to beat the hell out of them with his fists. He was a

mean man. You know?
And they used to fight like cats and dogs. Now Booker's mother was a very kind, beautiful woman, and as I told you, she was our music instructor at high school, and she allowed us to even drink.
Well I want to just digress a little bit.
